title: Evaluating a DAG
summary: What the runtime does with one committed reading. The middle row is the path of a message; its result, the new state, timers, intents and the checkpoint, commits in one transaction before the message is acknowledged. The top row is what interrupts or feeds that path, and a failing execution is suspended without stopping the others.

boxes.label: Committed telemetry
boxes.detail: One message per stored telemetry event: the device, its configuration and generation, and the readings with observed time and quality.

boxes.label: workflow-evaluator-v1
boxes.detail: A durable pull consumer with one message in flight and a 30-second acknowledgement wait. Geofence rules and DAGs share it. A message whose transaction fails is redelivered after a delay that doubles from 3 seconds to one minute, and evaluation reports as delayed meanwhile.

boxes.label: Checkpoint
boxes.detail: One row holds the stream's identity and the last evaluated sequence. A sequence at or below it is a redelivery and changes nothing; the next message must be exactly sequence + 1. A second guard remembers each event ID, so the same event is never evaluated twice.

boxes.label: Match executions
boxes.detail: Locks the organization's enabled executions and keeps those with a binding to the reading's device. Each one's bindings are checked again against the stored device: same configuration, same applied generation, no review required, parameter still mapped with the same type and unit.

boxes.label: Evaluate the plan
boxes.detail: Works on a copy of the state. Source nodes take the event's readings: good quality, right type, observed after activation and not in the future or historical. Then every node runs once in topological order. A value is known or unknown with a reason, and a source value turns unknown (stale) once its freshness passes.

boxes.label: Node catalogue
boxes.detail: Grouped as in the editor's palette. Inputs: source.parameter, constant. Calculations: math, convert. Conditions: compare, boolean, branch, hysteresis, geofence. Timing and correlation: window, join, sustained, cooldown. Actions: action.alert, action.event, action.command. All are versioned .v1. Sources, windows, hysteresis, sustained, cooldown and actions keep state between evaluations.

boxes.label: Timer sweep
boxes.detail: Each execution stores its next deadline: a window closing, a sustained condition coming due, a value going stale. When one is due the runtime records the stream's last sequence as a cutoff. Once the checkpoint has reached it, all enabled executions are evaluated with no event, and windows close only up to the recorded time. The cutoff is stored, so it survives a restart.

boxes.label: One transaction
boxes.detail: Writes each execution's new state, next timer and latest trace, a timeline entry (the newest 1,000 per workflow are kept), each new intent with its automation.intent.v1 outbox event, and the checkpoint. An intent's ID is a hash of the deployment, node and trigger, so the same trigger is recorded once.

boxes.label: Acknowledge
boxes.detail: The broker is told only after the database commit. If the runtime stops between the two, the message is redelivered and the checkpoint makes it a no-op.

boxes.label: Execution suspended
boxes.detail: A failed binding check or an evaluation error (binding_changed, a clock that moved backwards, more than 10,000 buffered samples on one source) disables that execution, records the evaluation as suspended and emits the event. The others are still evaluated and the transaction commits.

boxes.label: Dead letter
boxes.detail: A message that cannot be decoded is copied to the dead-letter stream with its consumer, sequence and error, the checkpoint moves past exactly that one sequence, and the message is acknowledged. One bad payload cannot hold up every organization's automations.

boxes.label: Paused until rebaseline
boxes.detail: If the stream is not the one the checkpoint was bound to, or the checkpoint is outside the retained sequences, evaluation pauses; devices, history and commands keep working. An operator accepts the gap with a reason: the checkpoint moves to the stream's last sequence, so the skipped readings are never evaluated. A rebaseline of a continuous checkpoint is refused.

steps.text: The consumer fetches one committed message. Nothing else is in flight.
Its stream sequence is compared with the checkpoint. A redelivery is skipped; anything but the next sequence is an error.
For a new event, the runtime locks the organization's enabled executions and keeps those bound to the reading's device.
If an execution's bindings still hold, its plan is evaluated: sources take the readings, then every node runs once in order.
Sixteen node types in five families. Stateful ones, such as windows, hysteresis and actions, carry their state from the previous evaluation.
The new state, the next timer, the trace, any action intents and the checkpoint are written in one transaction.
Only then is the message acknowledged. A crash before the acknowledgement redelivers a message the checkpoint already covers.
Time passes without telemetry too. A due timer waits until the readings already in the stream are consumed, then evaluates with no event.
If a binding changed or the evaluation fails, that execution is disabled and reported. It is one execution's problem, not the consumer's.
If the transaction itself fails, nothing is committed and the same message comes back after a growing delay.
A message that cannot be decoded is dead-lettered and the checkpoint steps over it.
If the stream was replaced or lost unevaluated readings, evaluation pauses until an operator rebaselines the checkpoint.
